thread.title: Stock Market Rebounds; Automaker Stocks Lead | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Stock Market Rebounds; Automaker Stocks Lead | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stock indexes opened higher Thursday and then piled on more gains in late morning trade. Automaker stocks led the pack, while utilities and food suffered dents.
X Utilities and food have posted the best daily gains for much of October. If the market turns north and stays on an upward course, more aggressive stocks are likely to lead.
The Nasdaq was up 2.7% as Thursday's session approached the midday mark. The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones industrial average added 1.8% and 1.5% respectively. Small caps, as measured by the Russell 2000, spurted 2.2%.
Volume rumbled higher on both major exchanges. Big percentage gains in rising volume point to institutional buying.
While Thursday morning's action was encouraging, big percentage gains intraday only served to set up ambushes in recent sessions. Market watchers will be studying today's close for signs of strength or weakness.

Ford ( F ) zoomed 7% in fast trade but remains 34% off its January high. Ford reported Q3 results late Wednesday, topping the Street's estimate by about 4%. CEO Jim Hackett said he would share more details in the near future about Ford's $11 billion turnaround plan.
Fiat Chrysler ( FCAU ) added 5% in strong volume but is 36% off its high. Fiat will release quarterly results Oct. 30.
The automaker group is a laggard, rating No. 183 among 192 industry groups, as of Wednesday's close.
Apple ( AAPL ) and the highly regarded FANG stocks rose but are mixed in relation to their recent highs. Facebook ( FB ) is 31% off its July high. Amazon.com ( AMZN ) is 15% off its September high. Netflix ( NFLX ) is 26% off its June high. Alphabet ( GOOGL ) is 15% off its July high. Apple is 5% off its high.
A stock has a better shot at a breakout if it is within 15% of its high.
Amazon To Report After today's close, Amazon and Alphabet will report quarterly results.
In the meantime, blue chips served up some solid gains. Microsoft ( MSFT ) jumped 5% after topping the consensus view on earnings by 19%. Intel ( INTC ) advanced 3.5%. Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) added 3%.
